identity.name: CENTURY PLYBOARDS (I) LTD
identity.industry: Building Materials / Engineered Wood & Interior Solutions

summary.oneLiner: Century Plyboards delivered record Q4 revenue (INR 1,492 cr, +24.5% YoY) and expanded EBITDA margins to 13.6% (ex-forex) driven by operating leverage and a turnaround in Laminates, while initiating strategic capex in Plywood and entering port logistics to secure supply chain advantages despite near-term chemical cost inflation.

one-line thesis: Century Plyboards delivered record Q4 revenue (INR 1,492 cr, +24.5% YoY) and expanded EBITDA margins to 13.6% (ex-forex) driven by operating leverage and a turnaround in Laminates, while initiating strategic capex in Plywood and entering port logistics to secure supply chain advantages despite near-term chemical cost inflation.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,492 cr (+24.5% YoY); EBITDA Margin: 13.6% ex-forex (up 150 bps QoQ); PAT: INR 268 cr (+44% YoY); Order Book: N/A (B2C/B2B inventory model); Net Debt: ~INR 1,600 cr (Debt/EBITDA ~2.5x gross, mgmt targets <1x long-term); One-offs: Mark-to-market forex losses on long-term debt obscured true profitability; normalized margins exclude these.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Muted 10-12% for Plywood next year due to high base; Margin: Targeting high-teens for MDF steady-state; Order Inflow: Stable demand post-price hikes; Capex: Focused on Hoshiarpur (Ply) and brownfield expansions, no frozen large capex for MDF/PB yet.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable; company operates on make-to-stock/distributor inventory model; management noted April sales remained robust despite March channel stocking.
segment / subsidiary detail: Plywood: Rev +17.9% YoY, EBITDA margin 16.1%; Laminates: Rev +16.3% YoY, margin turnaround to 10.3% (from 5.2% FY25); MDF: Rev +31% YoY, margin 11.3% (pressured by chemical costs/ATL spend); Particle Board: Rev +108% YoY, margin 7.2% (ramping new capacity).
growth verticals / optionality: Plywood capacity to increase 30% in FY27 (Hoshiarpur greenfield + brownfield); MDF brownfield debottlenecking (+60-70k cum) completing Q1FY27; Potential greenfield in UP/Orissa by FY28-29; Century Ports commenced operations (Khidderpore) targeting cash positivity in Q1FY27.
margins & cost dynamics: Input cost inflation (chemicals/resin) due to geopolitical conflicts; 15% price hike in MDF/Particle Board and 7% in Plywood implemented to cover costs; ATL spend in Q4 impacted MDF margins temporarily; timber prices stable.
capex / expansion: Primary focus on Plywood (Hoshiarpur plant, 48k CBM, Oct FY26); Brownfield expansions in Chennai/Kandla/Guwahati; Particle Board old plant scrapped; No frozen capex for MDF/PB beyond current debottlenecking; Funding via internal accruals.
capital allocation: Priority on sweating existing assets for ROCE improvement; Balance sheet discipline (targeting <1x long-term debt/EBITDA); Century Ports treated as separate profit center; No dividend/buyback specific commentary, focus on reinvestment for capacity.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical instability impacting chemical supply chains and forex volatility; Raw material price inflation outpacing pricing power; Execution risk on new greenfield projects; Competition in MDF leading to selective price rollbacks by peers.
management quality / tone: Confident on structural demand and brand equity; Cautious on providing specific FY27 guidance due to global fluidity (war/uranium mentions); Disciplined on capital allocation; Bullish long-term on MDF despite near-term noise.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly stated Century Ports provides no direct cost savings to the Ply business but serves as a separate profit center; Old Particle Board technology being completely scrapped rather than repurposed; Outsourcing in Plywood being phased out entirely for quality control despite capacity constraints.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising chemical/resin costs and supply chain disruptions | Greenply Industries | beneficiary | Med | Sector-wide price hikes (15% in MDF/PB, 7% in Ply) may improve industry realization if demand holds; Century's aggressive capacity expansion signals strong underlying demand benefiting peers with available capacity. |
| Import dependency for timber and chemicals | Saurashtra Cement | beneficiary | Low | Indirect beneficiary via broader infrastructure/logistics push; Century's port entry highlights value of logistics integration in building materials. |

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- The deck is organised around six reported revenue streams, each with its own volume and financial slide: Plywood (with Decoply and Commercial Veneer), Laminates, MDF (Plain and Prelam), Particle Board (Plain and Prelam), Logistics Services and "Others".
- Logistics Services is a genuinely different business inside the group - the deck shows it running at a gross profit of 81.3% of total income in FY2025-26 (vs 32.5% for the consolidated entity), on a much smaller base of Rs 159.07 crores total income.
- Century Ply Standalone is only part of the story: the Summary - Consolidated P&L slide reconciles the standalone entity to consolidated through a long list of subsidiaries - Auro Sundaram; Century Furniture; Ara, Arham, Apnapan, Adonis; Century Infotech; Century Panel; Century MDF; Century Infra; Century Pacific; Century Ports; and Century Gabon - together with their consolidation adjustments and non-controlling interests.
- Capital employed is now heavily panel-led: consolidated Fixed Assets grew from Rs 1,062.69 crores (2022-23) to Rs 2,809.40 crores (Q1 26-27), while shareholder's equity (including share capital of Rs 22.25 crores) went from Rs 1,910.62 crores to Rs 2,713.32 crores.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Myanmar impairment] "Extra-ordinary items in the FY 2022-23 pertains to impairment loss in our Myanmar subsidiary amounting to Rs 49.25 crores" - the write-off sits in the Plywood segment's financials.
- [Labour law / gratuity] "Exceptional items in FY 25-26 pertains to gratuity impact of labour law."
- [Entry tax settlement] "In FY 23-24 Sales and other expenses include Rs 7.13 crores towards settlement of Entry Tax Liability as per Amnesty Scheme of West Bengal Government."
- [Tax regime] "The company has opted for the new tax regime from the financial year 2021-22."
- [Presentation basis] The safe harbor states the figures are "re-grouped/re-casted/re-arranged for facilitating financial analysis and may not confirm to statutory formats" and that "All the figures except for the whole year are unaudited" - so these segment cuts are not the statutory numbers.
